subject: mathematics
question_text: If tan(A/2) = 5/6 and tan(C/2) = 2/5, determine the relation between a, b and c.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.125, chapter 12 PROPERTIES OF TRIANGLES, Very Short Answer question 15. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply the two given tangents
steps.margin_note: No separate mark at this length. The product of the two given tangents leaves the bracket of the MISSING angle: (s−b)/s.
steps.memory_tip: tan(A/2) tan(C/2) = (s−b)/s — the product keeps the letter of the angle that was NOT given.

recall.must_convey: That tan(A/2) tan(C/2) = (s−b)/s, because (s−a) and (s−c) cancel between the two roots.
accept: multiply the two half angle tangents and s minus a and s minus c cancel
the product is s minus b over s
the bracket left is the one for the angle not given
rendintini multiply cheste s minus b by s vasthundi
the product of tan half A and tan half C is s minus b over s

steps.why: Multiplying the two roots cancels (s−a) and (s−c) completely, leaving only the bracket of the angle that was NOT given. That is why the product picks out b.
common_mistakes: Adding the two tangents instead of multiplying them.

steps.label: Substitute the given values
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks. (5/6)(2/5) = 1/3, and clearing the fraction gives 3s − 3b = s, that is 2s = 3b.

accept: five sixths times two fifths is one third
so s minus b over s is one third and three s minus three b is s
that gives two s equals three b
one third vasthundi, so two s equals three b
clear the fraction to get two s equals three b

steps.why: The two given numbers multiply to a single fraction, and that fraction is a statement about s and b alone. Clearing it gives one plain equation between the perimeter and b.
common_mistakes: Writing s − b = 1/3 instead of (s − b)/s = 1/3.

steps.label: Check with the third half angle
steps.margin_note: No separate mark at this length. Because the three half angles add to 90°, the sum of the three pairwise products is 1, which fixes tan(B/2) = 20/37.
steps.memory_tip: The three half angles add to 90°, so the sum of their pairwise tangent products is 1.
lines: These three fix a : b : c = 87 : 74 : 61,

recall.must_convey: That the pairwise product identity fixes tan(B/2) = 20/37 and the sides in the ratio 87 : 74 : 61.
accept: the three half angles add to ninety so the pairwise products add to one
that fixes tan half B as twenty over thirty seven
the sides come out as eighty seven to seventy four to sixty one
moodu half angles ninety ki add authai, so pairwise products one
the third half angle is determined by the other two

steps.why: The two given tangents already fix the third, so the triangle is fixed up to size. Working it out gives the actual side ratio and confirms the relation found above.
common_mistakes: Using tan(A/2) + tan(B/2) + tan(C/2) = 1, which is not a standard result.

steps.label: State the relation
steps.margin_note: The other mark. 2s is the perimeter, so 2s = 3b reads a + b + c = 3b, and removing b gives a + c = 2b.
steps.memory_tip: 2s is the perimeter, so 2s = 3b means a + b + c = 3b and therefore a + c = 2b.
lines: 2s = a + b + c, so a + b + c = 3b

lines.text: ∴ a + c = 2b, so a, b, c are in A.P.

recall.must_convey: That 2s = a + b + c turns 2s = 3b into a + c = 2b, so a, b, c are in A.P.
accept: two s is the perimeter so a plus b plus c equals three b
take b off both sides to get a plus c equals two b
that means a b and c are in arithmetic progression
two s ante perimeter, so a plus c equals two b
the relation is a plus c equals two b
heard_as: a plus c equals two b

steps.why: 2s is the perimeter, so 2s = 3b says the perimeter is three times b. Taking b off both sides leaves a + c = 2b, which is exactly the condition for an arithmetic progression.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 2s = 3b without saying what it means for a, b and c.
Writing a + c = 3b by forgetting to remove b from the perimeter.
